title: A Stone Called Help
overview: After years of defeat, Israel turns away from other gods under Samuel's lead, wins an unexpected victory over the Philistines, and settles into a time of relative peace.

parts.label: The ark finds a home (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: After the deaths at Beth Shemesh in the previous chapter, a nearby town took in the ark, the sacred chest that stood for God's presence, and set apart a man named Eleazar to guard it. Twenty years passed before the people began to long for the LORD again, and the ark actually stayed there far longer, until King David moved it.

parts.label: Giving up other gods (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: Baal and Ashtoreth were the main god and goddess of the local Canaanite peoples, linked with rain, crops and fertility. Samuel tells Israel that truly coming back means dropping them completely and serving the LORD alone, and they do.

parts.label: Gathering at Mizpah (vv. 5-6)
parts.note: Samuel calls the nation together to pray, go without food and admit their wrongs, and from here he acts as Israel's judge, meaning its leader and settler of disputes. The text never explains why they poured out water; it was probably a sign of grief or of pouring out their hearts, but no one knows for sure.

parts.label: Thunder against the Philistines (vv. 7-11)
parts.note: The Philistines, a strong neighboring people who had been dominating Israel, saw the gathering as a threat and attacked while Israel was unprepared. Samuel offered a young lamb burned whole as a gift to God, and the text says the LORD answered with thunder that threw the Philistines into panic, after which Israel chased them down and killed many.

parts.label: The stone called Ebenezer (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: Ebenezer means "stone of help," the same name as the place where Israel was crushed and lost the ark a few chapters earlier, and many readers see the two as a pairing of defeat and rescue. The text says the Philistines stayed out and lost towns back to Israel, though later chapters show them still powerful, so this reads as a broad summary of Samuel's era.

parts.label: Samuel's years as leader (vv. 15-17)
parts.note: Each year Samuel traveled a loop of towns to hear cases and guide the people, then returned to his home in Ramah. He built an altar there, perhaps because the old worship center at Shiloh was no longer in use.

think: If you looked back over a hard stretch of your life, is there a moment you would mark with a stone, and what would you write on it?
